summary: Calling for "more goofy mysteries" is the right takeaway. The movie is a technical flex, a genuinely funny noir, and a chaos-machine that somehow keeps cartoons, humans, and detective plotting all on the same wavelength.
good_pick_if: you want something playful, inventive, and easy to watch with a group
maybe_skip_if: you want animation and live action kept in separate lanes

summary: The line "God is everywhere. You can feel Him" points to what people love here: a movie full of tactile beauty, spiritual ache, and tenderness that feels earned rather than sentimental.
good_pick_if: you want something gentle, emotional, and deeply felt
maybe_skip_if: you want a lighter family movie without sorrow in it

source_quotes.text: God is everywhere. You can feel Him

summary: The "most accurate portrayal of Batman ever" joke works because the movie actually understands the character: lonely, ridiculous, hyper-competent, and secretly desperate for connection under all the bits.
good_pick_if: you want a family movie that is fast, funny, and smarter than it has to be
maybe_skip_if: meta comedy and reference overload wear you out

source_quotes.text: the most accurate portrayal of batman ever

summary: The "be gay, (reluctantly) do crime" mood is basically the clean pitch. It is rambunctious, funny, and emotionally direct in a way that makes the outsider anger feel heartfelt instead of packaged.
good_pick_if: you want something funny, fast, and openly on the side of weird kids
maybe_skip_if: you want fantasy adventure without identity politics in the mix

summary: One review calls it a "stupidly intelligent meditation" hidden inside a goofy cartoon, which is why people get so attached to it. It is dreamy, funny, and much more philosophically slippery than its setup suggests.
good_pick_if: you want animation that gets weirder and smarter as it goes
maybe_skip_if: you want your comedy straightforward or fully explained

source_quotes.source: Letterboxd review by Super Delicious Planet Golden Special Reserve Gorgeous Aftercare Kit #69

summary: Calling it the "most mellow and romantic" Tsui Hark is useful because the movie really does float on softness, yearning, and a storybook prettiness that keeps the whole tragedy feeling luminous.
good_pick_if: you want a lush romance that feels dreamy more than literal
maybe_skip_if: you want your love stories grounded or unswoony

source_quotes.text: the most mellow and romantic Tsui Hark movie
source_quotes.source: Letterboxd review by Lou (rhymes with wow!)

summary: The joke that this is the "original Fast and the Furious" works because the whole cartoon is pure premise execution. It is fast, mean, and beautifully committed to turning repetition into elegance.
good_pick_if: you want a short burst of immaculate chase-comedy craft
maybe_skip_if: you need more than one recurring gag to stay engaged

source_quotes.text: This is the original Fast and the Furious.

summary: When people say there is "absolutely nothing holding this back from being a 5 star film," they mean it. The movie is goofy, quotable, and weirdly sincere about growing up without losing your whole SpongeBob brain.
good_pick_if: you want something loud, silly, and genuinely sweet underneath
maybe_skip_if: cartoon nonsense and meme-density are not your thing

source_quotes.text: absolutely nothing holding this back from being a 5 star film

summary: The phrase "staggeringly beautiful and immensely true" gets why this lingers. It is a handmade fantasy adventure with real visual grace, but it also knows how to turn storytelling and memory into emotional stakes.
good_pick_if: you want family fantasy that looks gorgeous and means it
maybe_skip_if: you want something looser or less emotionally earnest

summary: That feeling of being "nowhere near understanding how human minds were even capable of this" is the appeal. The movie is pure psychedelic design-play, Beatles mischief, and visual imagination running happily off the rails.
good_pick_if: you want something colorful, musical, and gloriously unbuttoned
maybe_skip_if: you want narrative clarity more than vibes and design

source_quotes.text: I'm nowhere near understanding how human minds were even capable of this
